categories.description: Use for rice-based and grain-based meals:

categories.name: Noodles & Soup
categories.description: Use for noodle-based or soup-based dishes:
examples: Pasta when it is primarily a noodle/pasta dish

categories.name: Meat & Seafood
categories.description: Use when meat, poultry, fish, or seafood is the MAIN food:

categories.name: Vegetables
categories.description: Use when vegetables are the MAIN food:
examples: Mixed vegetable dishes where vegetables are clearly the main component

categories.name: Fruits
categories.description: Use when fruit is the MAIN food:

categories.name: Bread & Pastry
categories.description: Use for bread, flatbread, bakery products and pastries:

categories.name: Snacks
categories.description: Use for smaller snack foods that are not primarily a full meal:

categories.name: Fast Food
categories.description: Use when the food is clearly a fast-food style meal:
examples: Pizza when clearly presented as fast-food style

categories.name: Desserts
categories.description: Use for sweet foods primarily eaten as dessert:
examples: Kuih dessert when clearly functioning as a dessert

categories.name: Drinks
categories.description: Use ONLY when the image is primarily a beverage:

categories.name: Dairy
categories.description: Use when dairy is the MAIN food:

categories.name: Other
categories.description: Use only when the food genuinely does not fit the categories above.

categoryGuidelines: Choose the category based on the MAIN food, not a minor ingredient.
Do not classify a rice meal as Meat & Seafood just because it contains chicken.
Do not classify a drink as Dairy just because it contains milk.
Do not classify every fried food as Fast Food.
Use Fast Food only when the food is clearly a fast-food-style product or meal.
Use Snacks for small snack foods.
Use Desserts for foods primarily intended as desserts.
Use Other only as a last resort.

healthTypes.name: Healthy
healthTypes.description: Generally nutrient-dense foods or balanced meals:
examples: Meals with vegetables and reasonable portions
Foods with relatively low added sugar and excessive oil

healthTypes.name: Moderate
healthTypes.description: Normal foods that can reasonably fit into a balanced diet but may contain significant calories, oil, carbohydrates, fat, sugar, or sodium.

healthTypes.name: Junk Food
healthTypes.description: Primarily highly processed, heavily fried, very sugary, or typical fast food with relatively low nutritional value.

healthTypeGuidelines: Do NOT classify something as Healthy merely because it contains vegetables.
Do NOT classify every fried food as Junk Food.
Consider the overall meal, cooking method, ingredients, portion, added oil, sugar, and nutritional balance.
When uncertain between Healthy and Junk Food, use Moderate.
